question.problem:
Find the shortest distance between the origin and the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=-\pi ,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨{sin}^{3}⁡t,{cos}^{3}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ T(-\pi ) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,-4⟩ \\ N(-\pi ) & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that  the position vector of the point where $t=-\pi $ is

$$
p=r(-\pi )=⟨{sin}^{3}⁡(-\pi ),{cos}^{3}⁡(-\pi ),\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\pi )⟩=⟨0,-1,1⟩.
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(-\pi )$ and the principal normal $N(-\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(-\pi )\times N(-\pi ) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,-4⟩\times ⟨-1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & -4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance between our plane and the origin is given by

$$
d=\frac{|(p-0)\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=\frac{|p\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=|p\cdot n|,
$$

since $‖n‖=1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|p\cdot n| \\  & =|⟨0,-1,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,3⟩| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}|\,0-4+3\,| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
